sections.overview: The Waved Umber is a geometrid moth found across much of Europe and into North Africa and western Asia.
sections.identification: Adults have a bark-like brown pattern and a wingspan of about 36–42 mm.
sections.habitat: It occurs in woodland, parks and gardens; French records also include edges and other planted places.
sections.diet: Its caterpillars feed on several woody plants, including privet and lilac; regional sources also report ash and blackthorn.
sections.behavior: Adults fly from spring into summer, with a partial second generation possible in favourable conditions in Belgium.
sections.reproduction: It overwinters as a pupa in a cocoon on its food plant.
sections.ecology: The larvae use a range of shrubs and trees, so the moth can occur in both semi-natural woodland and planted habitats.
sections.conservation: A Belgian catalogue lists it as Least Concern in Flanders (2023); this is a regional category, not a global assessment.
